what_its_for: Ivabradine is used to lower your heart rate if you have chronic heart failure or a certain type of abnormal heart rhythm where your heart beats too fast. It helps reduce the number of hospitalizations related to heart failure by slowing your heart down so it can pump more efficiently.
how_to_take: Take ivabradine by mouth with food, twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening with meals. Swallow the tablet whole or you may crush it and mix it with a small amount of water if needed. Always take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose (usually 5 mg twice daily) and may adjust it based on your heart rate and how well you tolerate the medicine. Your target resting heart rate is usually between 50 and 60 beats per minute. Do not change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time with your next meal. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store ivabradine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the level of ivabradine in your blood and cause side effects. Avoid taking St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) as it can make ivabradine less effective. Limit alcohol intake. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you notice changes in your vision, especially seeing halos or flashes of light, as ivabradine can temporarily affect your eyesight — particularly in low-light conditions.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a very slow heartbeat (less than 50 beats per minute), dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; irregular or pounding heartbeat; sudden worsening of shortness of breath or swelling in your legs; changes in your vision such as seeing halos, flashes, or blurry vision; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant, are planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding, as this medicine may not be safe.
when_it_works: Ivabradine begins to slow your heart rate within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take several weeks before you feel the full benefits, such as improved exercise tolerance and reduced symptoms of heart failure. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Ivabradine should NOT be used during pregnancy as it may harm the unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Do not breastfeed while taking ivabradine. Children: Ivabradine can be used in children 6 months and older for certain heart conditions, but only under close supervision of a pediatric heart specialist. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as slow heart rate and dizziness — use with caution and report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Liver or kidney disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as dose adjustments may be needed.
